sections.heading: Built-Up Roofing vs. Shingles: Roof Installation Choices for Montclair Homes

c.v: Are built-up roofs better than shingles?

runs.v: On a flat or low-slope roof, yes: built-up roofing is made for those roofs, while an asphalt shingle roof needs a slope of at least 2:12 under the International Residential Code. On a pitched house roof, shingles win, so most Montclair homeowners keep shingles on the main roof and let the crew install BUR or a single-ply membrane on the flat porch, garage, or rear addition, with step flashing where the flat roof meets the siding.

c.v: Each roof type has its place.

runs.v: Asphalt shingles are the most common roofing material; slate roofs can last over 100 years with proper maintenance, but slate tiles are heavier than asphalt shingles and require stronger support; and metal roofing systems are highly durable and energy-efficient, because metal roofs can reflect solar heat, reducing cooling costs. Newark Quality Roofing provides roof replacement services for aging roofs, and on a Montclair house a roof replacement can involve asphalt shingles or slate tiles, with every complete roof replacement tailored to local weather conditions.

c.v: What are the disadvantages of a built-up roof?

runs.v: Weight comes first: gravel surfacing adds several hundred pounds per 100 square feet, so the deck and framing must carry it. Hot-mopped installation brings asphalt fumes and odor to an occupied building and runs slower than a single-ply roof installation, a leak is harder to trace once water travels between plies, and loose gravel can clog drains and gutters.

Gutter installation ensures efficient stormwater drainage from roofs, gutter placement affects how well gutters lead stormwater away, and properly functioning gutters protect foundations from heavy rainfall. Aluminum gutters are long-lasting and less prone to leaks, and Yankee gutters are built into the roof for a discreet look. Newark Quality Roofing's gutter services include gutter installation and repairs to existing gutters below a built-up roof's scuppers.

faqs.q: How long does a built-up roof last on a Montclair building?

runs.v: About 30 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, against 15–25 years for EPDM and 7–20 years for TPO. The gravel surfacing shields the bitumen from UV radiation and impact, and periodic resurfacing of a sound BUR roof extends its life further, per NRCA maintenance guidance.

faqs.q: Should I restore or replace an aging built-up roof in Montclair?

runs.v: Restore it when the plies hold and the damage stays localized; replace it when damage exceeds 25–30% of the membrane or leaks recur at the same detail, the flat-roof threshold per Modernize and HomeGuide cost data. That is the 25% rule for roofing: once damage covers about a quarter of a roof, a new roof usually costs less over time than repeated repairs.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a built-up roof on a Montclair commercial building?

runs.v: Yes, once roof work on a commercial, multi-family, or attached building exceeds 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and the NJ Uniform Construction Code; confirm the filing with the Township of Montclair construction office before work begins. Full removal to the deck applies when the existing roof is water-soaked or already carries 2 or more layers, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4, while a detached one- or two-family reroof counts as ordinary maintenance and requires no permit.

faqs.q: Does a built-up roof in a Montclair historic district need extra approval?

runs.v: It can. A property in a historic district, or a designated landmark, can need extra review before exterior roofing that changes its appearance, so confirm the parcel's status with the Township of Montclair before work begins. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private owner.
